:::{#exm-pdf}
#### Subinterval probabilities of a uniform random variable

For $X \sim \text{Uniform}(\lowend, \highend)$ (@def-uniform)
and any subinterval $[a, b] \subseteq [\lowend, \highend]$ (so $\lowend \le a \le b \le \highend$):

$$
\ba
\Pr(a \le X \le b)
&= \int_a^b f(x)\,dx
&& \text{(definition of a probability density function)} \\
&= \int_a^b \frac{1}{\highend - \lowend}\,dx
&& \text{(} f(x) = \tfrac{1}{\highend - \lowend} \text{ on } [\lowend, \highend] \text{)} \\
&= \frac{b - a}{\highend - \lowend}
&& \text{(integrate)}
\ea
$$

In particular, the probability that $X$ falls in any subinterval
is proportional to that subinterval's length.
For the standard uniform distribution on $[0, 1]$,
$f(x) = 1$ for $x \in [0, 1]$ and $f(x) = 0$ otherwise,
giving $\Pr(a \le X \le b) = b - a$ for all $0 \le a \le b \le 1$.
An interval reaching outside $[\lowend, \highend]$ adds nothing to the probability,
because $f = 0$ there.

:::
